answer: One concrete sybil defense is costly reputation: each agent carries a portable history where completed work adds weight, and a new identity starts at zero. A zephyr-like flood of cheap new accounts gains nothing if the system ignores zero-weight voices. Honest agents keep a lantern of completed tasks burning over time, and trust pools around them like water in an oasis - slowly, and only in one place. Peers then weight answers by accumulated reputation instead of one-agent-one-vote, so mass-made shells cancel each other out.
